# moddotplot-rs v0.2.0-beta.4

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

This fourth 0.2 beta makes compressed whole-genome input practical and validates eager
retention of a complete diploid human assembly. It remains a functional preview for
scientific evaluation. This release is tagged locally; nothing is deployed, uploaded,
or published by the release process.

## Highlights

* BGZF FASTA and annotation streams are detected from their headers and decompressed
  block-by-block with bounded parallelism while preserving record order.
* FASTA uptake uses table-driven eight-base packing, larger Wasm handoffs, compacted
  record storage, and throttled progress reporting for substantially faster loading.
* The Wasm session admission budget is 3 GiB so complete diploid human assemblies can
  remain resident even if the original file changes after loading.
* A constant-time two-level sparse invalid-base bit vector replaces the dense validity
  bitmap, retaining only blocks containing ambiguity or gap positions.
* Plain gzip and BGZF BED, GFF3, and GTF annotation imports share the corrected
  compressed-stream handling.

## Whole-genome validation

The supplied HG002 v1.2 BGZF multi-FASTA contains 47 records and 5,999,430,218 bases.
In installed Google Chrome on the release host, every record was retained in 28.0
seconds, the initial self-dotplot reached Ready in 35.8 seconds, and reported
application memory was approximately 1.52 GiB.

## Scientific compatibility

The dotplot estimator, heatmap values, and default scientific configuration are
unchanged from v0.2.0-beta.3. The 256-register preview and 1,024-register detailed
configuration digests remain `58e084b7190f4d93` and `bc5c5131ad1c9a20`, respectively.
The beta.1 [validation record](v0.2.0-beta.1/VALIDATION.md) remains the numerical
evidence for those configurations.

## Verification

* Rust formatting, strict Clippy checks, the workspace test suite, and wasm32
  compilation pass.
* All 33 TypeScript unit tests and the production browser build pass.
* A real-file installed-Chrome test retained and plotted the complete supplied HG002
  diploid assembly.
* Documentation generation and local-link checks pass.

## Known limitations

* The release remains a functional preview, not research-validated software.
* Wasm32 has a 4 GiB linear address-space ceiling; the 3 GiB application admission
  budget reserves space for allocator, stack, transient, and plotting allocations.
* BigWig, BigBed, VCF, and indexed remote annotation sources are not supported.
* Imported annotations and loaded sequences are session-local and are discarded on
  reload.
* Approximate identity below roughly 80% remains outside the target operating regime.
* Numeric/high-resolution image export and stable numeric/pixel goldens remain open
  work.
